# gamenight

<!-- badges: start -->

<!-- badges: end -->

**gamenight** helps you choose a game for your game night. Tell it how
many people are playing, how much time you have and the age of the
youngest player, and it finds well-rated games that fit, and shows how
much better your options get if you allow more time.

Documentation
website:<https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-noormoolji17/>

## Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-noormoolji17")
```


## Launch the app

``` r
gamenight::run_app()
```

The app is for **someone hosting a game night**, and answers the
question: *for my group's size and ages, how much time do we need to
allow to play a really well-rated game?*

## Find games from the console

`find_games()` returns the games that suit your group, best rated first:

```{r example}
library(gamenight)

find_games(players = 2, max_minutes = 30, youngest_age = 8) |>
  head(5)
```

## The data

The package includes `games`: 20,309 tabletop games (board, card, dice
and party games) with their player counts, playing times, suggested
minimum ages and ratings. The data comes from
[BoardGameGeek](https://boardgamegeek.com), via the [Kaggle
BoardGameGeek Reviews
dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jvanelteren/boardgamegeek-reviews)
by Jesse van Elteren, as prepared for [TidyTuesday on 25 January
2022](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2022/2022-01-25).
The script that downloads and cleans it is in `data-raw/games.R`. See
`?games` for what each column means and how the data was cleaned.
